questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language (english) and the fact that I've always wanted to try to study in the US.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been the best experience! I am so glad I was given the opportunity to go!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult sometimes but it always worked out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person we could always email, and also the professors were very helpful in regards to signing up for clases etc., as well as the other students (also the other danish exchange students were a great resource).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy through a facebook group (or at least doable), they are having a bit of a housing crisis in SB right now, but it worked out for all of the danish exchange students/we all found housing on our own except two, they went with campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's much more affortable (campus housing is very expensive!) and in general a better experience, I would say (at least in SB), because you live with people more your own age and the area is so nice, closer to the beach and even closer to campus than some of the campus housing spots.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The place I got was pretty good but I think I was lucky too.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It will work out in the end, but(!) their regristration system is pretty different and a bit stressful. If you text the professor and tell them you are a exchange student it can help a lot because you are first in line if the class is full as a foreign student.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can only sign up for two classes at a time within a certain window of time and therefore many of the popular classes is already full when you get to the next round of signing-up. Prioritize your most important classes in the first round!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email the professor!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure which classes you can get transferred back home before you sign up! Then it should be pretty easy to get them (it is harder/very hard to change classes after the registration period!).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Perfect fit!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Same level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked it better, actually, at UCSB because you had different assignments during the quarter which all added up to the final grade compared to the one final grade at UCPH. This made me put in more effort during the whole quarter and not just in the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PSY 108, PSY 142, and COMM 122 (this was first quarter, winter quarter).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PSY 142 very interessting and with a great professor wellknown for this field and her research (I was star strucked!).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The housing is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The books! Almost all the teachers oploaded them as a pdf-files. Don't buy book in the bookstore, it's so expensive, buy them used or at amazon, if you have to buy them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many great opportunities in the SB area (that being clubs, sports, parties, etc.).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Recreation Center provided by the University is a great place that offers facilities for all different kinds of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Excursion Club" is a great way to meet new people and they have a bunch of great trips every week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The ocean, the mountains, and the nature in general.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! People are very welcoming, outgoing, and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: "Excursion Club" and housing is the best way. Your roomies/housemates is the key to the social life.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You are not that close with your classmates in the classes you take because everybody make their own scedule with classes and it gets pretty mixed up.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social, outgoing american culture is great for exchange. It's easy to make new friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in Isla Vista instead of Campus Housing, be prepared to spend around 150.000 DKK (it's expensive and fun to travel aorund too), sign up for "Excursion Club".

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The preparations before you go is hard but it's worth it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature and the friendly people!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money ... it is pretty expensive, and the registration for classes can be pretty stressful too.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Santa Barbara is the best UC college!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
